raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through for this year.

I've been farming these 6 mu for decades now — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same as everyone around here. At my age and with just 6 mu, I'm not trying to do anything fancy. I just want a steady harvest so the family has grain and a bit of cash. Two of us are mostly on the farm; my son works in town and helps on weekends during the busy times.

**Wheat (the winter crop):**
I'll plant around October 10th, right when the neighbors do. I use an improved variety from the agricultural supply shop — something like Jimai 22, costs me maybe 8 yuan per mu for seed since I buy certified, not saved. Before planting I spread compound fertilizer, about 40 kg/mu of 15-15-15, and work it in with the rotary tiller. That gives roughly 6 kg N from the base. Then at jointing in early March I topdress urea, about 25 kg/mu — that's another 11-12 kg N. Total N works out to around 17-18 kg/mu. The extension guy says 15 is enough but I've always done a little more and my wheat looks better for it. 

Irrigation: I'll water before the ground freezes (winter watering), then at jointing, and again at grain filling. Three times usually. The well is metered so I can't be wasteful. If spring rains come I might skip one.

I spray herbicide once in spring for weeds, and if I see aphids at heading I'll spray once more. Harvest in early June with a hired combine — costs me about 50 yuan/mu but saves my back.

I expect around 450 kg/mu if the weather cooperates.

**Maize (summer crop):**
The minute the wheat combine is off the field I need to plant maize — one week, no more. I use a no-till planter service; the operator comes through with a seeder that drops seed right into the wheat stubble. Costs me around 30 yuan/mu including seed (hybrid, Zhengdan 958 type). No tillage, saves time and moisture.

For fertilizer I use one-time application with the planter — about 50 kg/mu of a slow-release compound. That's maybe 15 kg N/mu, plus P and K. I don't topdress maize separately — too much walking in the field when it's tall, and at my age I prefer one-shot.

Irrigation depends on July-August rain. Usually I water once at the big trumpet stage if it's dry. If rains are good, zero times.

Spray herbicide once early for weeds between the rows. Pests I watch for borers but usually don't spray.

Harvest late September with a hired picker. Expect about 500 kg/mu.

**Overall thinking:**
With only 6 mu I can't afford bad choices but I also can't afford to chase the highest yields — the extra cost isn't worth it on this scale. I stick with what's worked. Biggest risks are drought in May for the wheat and a wet autumn for the maize. Total cash I need to put out is maybe 2,500-3,000 yuan for the year including hired machinery.
